findings.expected: OD-6 excludes a misread only when it changes the object or difficulty. In this recipe 'no real solution' is one of the two designed outcomes (6 of 12 target keys). A misread that keeps the canonical decision (real->real, or no-real->no-real, e.g. a dropped/added sign on an out-of-range target) leaves the object and difficulty unchanged, so it is an OD-6 misread: raw 3, MR-1 -> 2/3.
findings.actual: The shared line copied into this recipe says 'misreads that change the object or difficulty (including making the task easier or leaving no solution) receive normal canonical marking'. Read literally, (3,-3pi/4) misread as 3pi/4 with '3pi/4 > pi/2, so no real solution' 'leaves no solution' and is marked canonically: P-B1 and P-M1 need the actual target and P-A1 needs a supporting comparison, so 0/3. The same sign misread on a real target (-pi/6 -> pi/6) gets 2/3. The exemplar (:53) and fixtures cover only no-real -> real (no MR) and a k misread.
findings.evidence: Own marking tests above (2/3 vs 0/3); Cambridge PDF 3 wording 'object and difficulty of the question remain unaltered'; OD-6 record lists 'leaves no solution' as an example of a change, which it is not when the canonical task already has no real solution.
findings.repair: Add one sentence to the principal work order and exemplar: 'Here no real solution is a designed outcome: a misread that keeps the canonical decision (real->real or no-real->no-real) is an OD-6 misread; one that flips the decision changes the object and is marked canonically.' Add fixtures (3,-3pi/4) read as 3pi/4 -> 2/3 and (2,pi/3) read as 2pi/3 -> canonical. Judgement at the margin: a careful reader can reach 2/3 from 'change the object', but the example as written points the other way on half the target keys.

findings.expected: E/F fixtures state the OD-6 classification and canonical marks for misreads that land on cases the domain itself treats as degenerate or excluded.
